title: Inference provider competitive triage and market momentum tracker
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a continuous, lightweight program to triage inference providers and open-model entrants against Redwood’s product priorities and create an operational momentum signal that feeds product, sales, and ops. We need a repeatable rubric that combines availability, latency-cost delta, API stability, quantization/compatibility risk, and enterprise fit signals (compliance, regional footprint). Deliverables: 1) daily momentum dashboard with trend scores, 2) weekly prioritized watchlist (top 25 candidates) with tradeoff notes and migration impact estimates, 3) a short playbook for Solutions/Sales for how to use the watchlist in procurement conversations, 4) a lightweight monthly brief for execs highlighting emergent risks/opportunities. This ticket covers the PM scope: rubric, data sources, dashboard spec, and stakeholder onboarding; engineering tickets will be spawned for instrumentation and dashboard implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented and reviewed: availability, latency-cost delta, API contract drift, quantization compatibility, enterprise readiness (security/compliance/region).

Data sources mapped and accessible: provider status pages, synthetic latency benchmarks (short/long context), usage telemetry (beta customers), model-card parsing for quantization flags, public release cadence.
Momentum dashboard spec (fields, aggregation, refresh cadence, alert thresholds) uploaded to Confluence and reviewed by Eng/Analytics/GTMS.
Weekly watchlist template created with required fields (score breakdown, migration effort estimate, fallback compatibility suggestions) and tested with 3 real examples.
Playbook for Sales/Solutions drafted and validated in two customer-facing mock-ups.
comments: 2025-10-18 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff completed; initial stakeholder list includes Analytics, Runtime Eng, Solutions, Legal. Agreed minimum-viable rubric. Action: PM to mock rubric, Eng to scope synthetic job.

2025-11-02 | Luca Moreno: Prototype synthetic workload running on internal clusters (short/long contexts). Early signal: Provider X shows 22% higher token-latency under 2k context. Need normalization method.
2025-12-05 | Sarah Kim (Analytics): Proposed normalization by p50+p95 delta vs our baseline rather than absolute latency; reduces noise from infra spikes.
2026-01-12 | Legal (James Ortega): Noted that extracting model-cards from provider website may raise TOS questions; recommend linking rather than scraping for now. Added to risk log.
2026-02-20 | Solutions (Maya Desai): Reviewed watchlist template; suggested an added column with 'migration psychological cost' (buyer friction) for sales narratives. Included in template.
2026-03-03 | Luca Moreno: Dashboard wireframe reviewed in sync; Eng to deliver first-pass API for momentum scores by 2026-03-18.
risks: Public scraping of provider sites may violate TOS; fallback to manual linking and vendor outreach is slower.
Synthetic benchmarks may not reflect customer workloads—need to validate against three distinct field workloads before using as single signal.
Score volatility during provider release weeks may create false positives; smoothing window required.
